A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Infinite Horizon Markov Economies and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–C. Content can be matched reliably across pagination and editorial changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original simulations comparing GAPNet with neural projection on deterministic and stochastic exchange economies, with outcomes in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: The original exchange-economy simulations and GAPNet versus neural-projection results remain in Section 5, Appendix C, and Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: The Markov economy model, exploitability objective, policy parameterization, TTSSGDA algorithm, and GAPNet approach are retained. Expanded explanations and revised mathematical statements do not document a changed computational procedure or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate linear, Cobb–Douglas, and Leontief exchange economies under the same deterministic and stochastic transition scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neural projection, also identified as deep equilibrium nets, remains the comparator in both transition scenarios and all utility classes. Figures 1–2 retain the same GAP and NPM comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 retains the economy sizes, 30-step simulation horizon, 1000-episode tuning, 2000-episode final training, learning rates, sampling budgets, and normalization procedure. The same three evaluation metrics are used.

E4.justification: The deterministic/stochastic and utility-class comparisons are retained. Neither version adds ablations, sensitivity tests, error analyses, or case studies beyond the existing experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Sampling 50 policies for metric normalization is documented identically in Appendix C.3.

E6.justification: Corresponding curves in Figures 1–2 retain the same values, trajectories, and method rankings. No result entries are added or removed; the horizontal axes are relabeled in iteration units.

T1.justification: v2 adds value-function equalities, adds 'for all states' to Lemma 3's probabilistic bound, and corrects variable use in Lemma 4 and Theorem C.1. Core proofs and convergence rates remain substantially unchanged. Appendix B.2's separately labeled existence corollary repackages an existing argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same main contributions: Markov pseudo-games, equilibrium existence, the exchange-economy reduction, polynomial-time stationarity guarantees, and empirical GAPNet effectiveness.

C2.justification: The discussion following Theorem 3.2 and expanded Theorem 4.2 explicitly distinguish finite-time proximity to approximate stationarity from exact necessary conditions in the limit. Section 5 reframes near-zero exploitability as approximating necessary RRE conditions rather than approximating a Radner equilibrium.

D1.justification: Footnote 22 and Appendix C.4 replace the anonymous code-repository address with a named GitHub repository. Implementation, hyperparameter, software, and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to equilibrium theory, macroeconomics, and reinforcement learning remain unchanged, including Appendix A. Bibliographic differences mainly reflect updated page references.

P1.justification: v2 locally edits prose and terminology and expands explanations of history distributions, parameterization, and convergence guarantees. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 add explicit Iterations and Normalized Values axis labels and replace index ticks with iteration counts. Figure sizing, placement, and the Figure 1 caption also change, while the same panels and curves are retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit plot axes and clearer convergence qualifications improve readability. However, new Equation (3) leaves the normalization of conditioning on the initial state unclear, and Lemma 3 adds an all-states probability claim without a corresponding proof revision. These mathematical concerns offset identifiable explanatory gains, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
